speaker: Unknown
en: For two decades, the cloud has been shaped by human developers writing code and managing its deployment.
zh: 二十年来，云一直是由人类开发者编写代码并管理其部署所塑造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now a growing share of production code is generated by LLMs with little human review.
zh: 现在，越来越大部分的生产代码是由 LLM 生成的，几乎没有人工审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that code is not fully trusted, it increasingly runs in isolated, sandboxed environments.
zh: 因为这些代码不被完全信任，它们越来越多地运行在隔离的、沙箱化的环境中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meanwhile, AI agents are starting to operate infrastructure directly by spinning services up and tearing them down on their own.
zh: 与此同时，AI 智能体开始直接操作基础设施，自行启动和关闭服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Together, these shifts raise the question of whether the cloud needs to be rebuilt for machine operators rather than humans.
zh: 这些变化加在一起提出了一个问题：云是否需要为机器操作者而不是人类而重建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Render is a cloud platform designed for application deployment by handling scaling, self-healing, and security to reduce operations work.
zh: Render 是一个为应用部署设计的云平台，通过处理扩缩容、自愈和安全来减少运维工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Render has been adapting to the AI era by building tools that let agents deploy and debug applications directly with added guardrails and security.
zh: Render 一直在适应 AI 时代，通过构建让智能体直接部署和调试应用的工具，并附加护栏和安全措施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anurag Gohl is the founder and CEO of Render.
zh: Anurag Gohl 是 Render 的创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, Anurag joins Sean Falconer to discuss why so many teams end up rebuilding the same infrastructure on top of Kubernetes, what changes when AI agents become first-class users of infrastructures and the guardrails that shift demands, and why the economics of AI are pushing developers towards higher-level platforms that trade fine-grained control for speed and safety.
zh: 在本期节目中，Anurag 与 Sean Falconer 一起讨论为什么这么多团队最终在 Kubernetes 之上重建相同的基础设施、当 AI 智能体成为基础设施的一等用户时会发生什么变化、以及护栏如何转变需求，还有为什么 AI 的经济学正在推动开发者转向更高级别的平台，用细粒度控制换取速度和安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is hosted by Sean Falconer.
zh: 本期节目由 Sean Falconer 主持。

speaker: Unknown
en: Check the show notes for more information on Sean's work and where to find him.
zh: 更多关于 Sean 工作的信息以及在哪里可以找到他，请查看节目说明。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anurag, welcome to the show.
zh: Anurag，欢迎来到节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, Sean.
zh: 谢谢你，Sean。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been looking forward to this.
zh: 我一直很期待这次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I wanted to go back a little bit in time and ask you a little bit about your history and maybe how some of those experiences led you to the founding, render, and everything that you're doing there today.
zh: 所以我想稍微回到过去，问你一些关于你的历史的问题，也许还有那些经历如何让你创立了 Render，以及你今天在那里所做的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you were roughly, I think, around like the eighth employee at Stripe?
zh: 所以你大概是，我记得，大约是 Stripe 的第八号员工？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by the time you left, how many engineers were managing AWS?
zh: 那么到你离开的时候，有多少工程师在管理 AWS？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess what did that experience teach you about cloud complexity and the actual cost companies are putting into just simply managing this beast of the cloud?
zh: 我想，那段经历让你对云的复杂性以及公司仅仅为了管理云这个庞然大物所投入的实际成本有什么认识？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so at all times when I was at Stripe, around 15 to 20% of the engineering team was simply managing VMs on AWS and all the complexity around that, storage and networking.
zh: 是的，我在 Stripe 期间，工程团队一直有大约 15% 到 20% 仅仅是在管理 AWS 上的 VM 以及围绕它的所有复杂性，存储和网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: load balancing and it didn't really get easier and obviously as Stripe's scale grew the complexity increased and you needed to continue to hire people to continue to help you scale and it just never stopped.
zh: 负载均衡，而且它并没有变得更容易，显然随着 Stripe 规模的增长，复杂性也增加了，你需要继续招人继续帮助你扩容，而且它从未停止过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think if you think about Stripe or even other examples of great engineering organizations like that, they're probably one of the best engineering organizations in the world.
zh: 我还认为，如果你想想 Stripe，甚至其他类似伟大工程组织的例子，它们可能是世界上最好的工程组织之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they're running into this problem, clearly it's a problem that's going to essentially impact everyone if they can't figure this thing out.
zh: 而如果连它们都遇到这个问题，很明显，如果它们都解决不了这个问题，这基本上就是一个会影响到所有人的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and just to be clear, I do think that Stripe did the best they could at that time because that was really the only way for them to run in the cloud reliably and scalably.
zh: 是的，需要说明的是，我确实认为 Stripe 在当时已经尽力了，因为那确实是他们能在云上可靠且可扩展地运行的唯一方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as technology changed, as containerization took hold,
zh: 但是随着技术的变化，随着容器化的兴起，

speaker: Unknown
en: It became clearer to me, and I'm talking about the 2017, 2016 era when a lot of people were containerizing their apps, but then they had to deal with Kubernetes complexity to actually run these containers in production in a way that was scalable or secure or reliable.
zh: 对我来说变得更清楚了，我说的是 2016、2017 年那个时代，当时很多人在把他们的应用容器化，但他们随后不得不应对 Kubernetes 的复杂性，才能以可扩展、安全或可靠的方式在生产环境中运行这些容器。

speaker: Unknown
en: It became clear to me that you could give app developers, and specifically app developers, not DevOps engineers, because Render has always focused on application developers.
zh: 对我来说变得清楚的是，你可以赋予应用开发者——具体来说是应用开发者，而不是 DevOps 工程师，因为 Render 一直专注于应用开发者——

speaker: Unknown
en: You could give application developers the same powers that they would get from the most accomplished world-class internal DevOps team, and you could do it in a way that was entirely self-serve for them.
zh: 你可以赋予应用开发者与世界上最有成就的世界级内部 DevOps 团队同等的能力，而且你可以以一种对他们来说完全自助的方式来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they could simply focus on pushing their code and then get out of the box primitives for scaling, for self-healing, for all kinds of state management.
zh: 他们只需专注于推送代码，然后就能获得开箱即用的原语，用于扩缩容、自愈以及各种状态管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they would get, you know, effectively one of the best DevOps teams in the world productized.
zh: 而他们会得到的，你知道，实际上就是世界上最好的 DevOps 团队之一被产品化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what Render ended up becoming.
zh: 这就是 Render 最终成为的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I guess like before kind of getting into specifics on render, what kind of breaks down?
zh: 是的，我想在深入讨论 Render 的细节之前，究竟是什么出了问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you have people using containers, using containerized orchestration platforms that are well sort of established in the industry like Kubernetes, but at the same time, it seems like at scale, that's a very hard thing to just manage.
zh: 比如你有人们在用容器，用业内已相当成熟的容器编排平台比如 Kubernetes，但与此同时，似乎在规模化时，这是一件非常难以管理的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So given that there's all this industry investment into Kubernetes, like what is it that specifically kind of breaks down as teams start to try to scale the management of that?
zh: 那么考虑到业界在 Kubernetes 上有这么多投入，当团队开始尝试扩展对它的管理时，具体是什么出了问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we do manage a lot of Kubernetes clusters ourselves, and we see this firsthand.
zh: 是的，我们自己确实管理着很多 Kubernetes 集群，我们亲眼看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it all depends on what kind of application architecture you're working with.
zh: 我认为这完全取决于你在处理什么样的应用架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's a really simple application, then it can run anywhere.
zh: 如果是一个非常简单的应用，那它可以在任何地方运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can run on Kubernetes, it can run on Heroku, it can run on other cloud providers.
zh: 它可以在 Kubernetes 上运行，可以在 Heroku 上运行，可以在其他云提供商上运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as you start to become
zh: 但当你开始变得

speaker: Unknown
en: Bigger if your business is growing.
zh: 更大，如果你的业务在增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: You start needing more configuration around which applications can talk to each other.
zh: 你开始需要更多配置来规定哪些应用可以互相通信。

speaker: Unknown
en: You start needing the notion of CICD needs to work in a certain way.
zh: 你开始需要 CI/CD 以某种特定方式运作的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to have certain environments be protected.
zh: 你需要让某些环境受到保护。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need certain services to be not available to the internet.
zh: 你需要某些服务不对互联网开放。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need observability across all of this.
zh: 你需要对所有这些有可观测性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you need to be aware of when something goes down, you need to get alerted, and then you need to go solve that problem yourself because you have to then understand, well, you stood up on Kubernetes and you need to understand sometimes exactly how Kubernetes works under the hood to know, well, this network policy change is what caused this DNS error.
zh: 然后你需要知道什么时候什么东西挂了，你需要收到告警，然后你需要自己去解决这个问题，因为你必须搞明白，嗯，你在 Kubernetes 上搭建了东西，有时你需要确切理解 Kubernetes 在底层是如何工作的，才能知道，嗯，是这个网络策略变更导致了这个 DNS 错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with Kubernetes, you have to manage all of these things yourself.
zh: 而用 Kubernetes，你必须自己管理所有这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You spin up
zh: 你启动

speaker: Unknown
en: Even on quote-unquote managed Kubernetes clusters, you have to write a lot of YAML by hand that describes how to deploy your applications.
zh: 即使在所谓的托管 Kubernetes 集群上，你也必须手写大量 YAML 来描述如何部署你的应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: But really what that YAML is doing is describing a lot of the internals of the Kubernetes architecture and the Kubernetes concepts themselves.
zh: 但实际上这些 YAML 所做的，是在描述 Kubernetes 架构的许多内部机制以及 Kubernetes 概念本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as your application scales, things become bottlenecks.
zh: 然后随着你的应用程序扩展，一些东西会成为瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have to kind of manage those bottlenecks by understanding exactly what that is.
zh: 然后你就必须通过准确理解那到底是什么来管理这些瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might never have encountered it, but suddenly you have a lot of internal DNS traffic because your application grew and now your core DNS isn't working anymore.
zh: 你可能从来没遇到过这种情况，但突然间你有了大量内部 DNS 流量，因为你的应用程序增长了，而现在你的核心 DNS 不工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, who takes care of that?
zh: 那么，谁来负责处理这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have to go figure out how to configure core DNS to serve all that traffic.
zh: 然后你就得去研究如何配置 core DNS 来服务所有这些流量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's every layer of the infrastructure stack within Kubernetes and even below it because you also have to figure out how to keep your VMs patched when things happen and you have to deal with node pools and you have to configure different nodes for different things and you have to make sure that your nodes are also well utilized.
zh: 所以这是 Kubernetes 内部基础设施栈的每一层，甚至是它下面的层，因为你还必须搞清楚在发生事情时如何保持你的虚拟机打好补丁，你必须处理节点池，你必须为不同的用途配置不同的节点，你还必须确保你的节点得到良好的利用。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to pay for a lot of extra capacity because that's what Kubernetes likes to do and you end up spending way more on just managing lots of unused Kubernetes capacity
zh: 你必须为大量额外的容量付费，因为这就是 Kubernetes 喜欢做的事情，最终你会在管理大量闲置的 Kubernetes 容量上花费多得多的钱

speaker: Unknown
en: Just so you can deploy your application the next time.
zh: 只是为了你下次能部署你的应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think companies end up spending a lot of time on COGS optimization because their cloud bills grow escalating and getting out of control.
zh: 然后我认为公司最终会在 COGS 优化上花大量时间，因为他们的云账单不断攀升、失控。

speaker: Unknown
en: I made this point recently about sort of data infrastructure where we have all these great data tools today, but
zh: 我最近提到过关于数据基础设施的一点，就是我们今天有这么多出色的数据工具，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: The complexity of actually managing our data has not decreased as we've gotten better tooling.
zh: 实际管理我们数据的复杂性并没有随着工具变好而降低。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually gotten harder because there's just simply more data, there's more complexity involved, and now we have a bunch of tools that we also have to understand how those things fit together.
zh: 实际上变得更难了，因为数据更多了，涉及的复杂性更多了，而现在我们又多了一堆工具，我们还必须理解这些东西如何拼合在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds like the same problem when it comes to managing network infrastructure.
zh: 听起来在管理网络基础设施上也是同样的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have all these great tools, we have elastic scalability, but...
zh: 我们有这么多出色的工具，我们有弹性伸缩，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of complexity making this sort of juggernaut of different services work together at a reasonable way, especially at scale.
zh: 要让这一大堆不同的服务以一种合理的方式协同工作，其中有大量的复杂性，尤其是在大规模场景下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, exactly.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And different parts of your application might scale differently.
zh: 而且你应用程序的不同部分可能以不同的方式扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you just have to manage all of that across the board.
zh: 所以你必须全面管理所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even understanding Kubernetes is not something you can sort of just do.
zh: 而且即使是理解 Kubernetes 也不是你随便就能做到的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't really build your Kubernetes YAMLs using AI because AI makes mistakes and you have to understand when it does make a mistake because something will stop working at 2 a.m. at night and then AI won't really be able to tell you
zh: 你不能真正用 AI 来构建你的 Kubernetes YAML，因为 AI 会犯错，而当它犯错时你必须能够理解，因为某个东西会在凌晨 2 点停止工作，然后 AI 其实没办法告诉你

speaker: Unknown
en: What it should change?
zh: 它应该改什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you just wrote it with AI, you have no idea how the thing works, and then you don't really want to be vibe coding your infrastructure when something's down.
zh: 因为那东西就是你用 AI 写的，你完全不知道它是怎么工作的，而在有东西宕机的时候，你肯定不想用 vibe coding 的方式来搞你的基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I would think that I'm sure we'll touch on AI because you can't really have a conversation in technology without talking about AI these days.
zh: 是啊，我敢肯定我们会聊到 AI，因为如今谈技术就不可能不谈 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as people are using AI to generate more code, we're creating essentially more abstraction from the details of the code.
zh: 但随着人们用 AI 生成越来越多的代码，我们实际上在代码细节之上创造了更多抽象。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's going to be, I think, more buffer between really understanding the deep internals of how that thing was built and run in the interest of essentially speed, which then when things go wrong, of course, makes it even harder to kind of debug and understand what's going on.
zh: 所以我认为，为了本质上追求速度，在真正理解那个东西的深层内部机制、它是如何构建和运行之间，会有更多缓冲地带，而当出问题时，这当然会让调试和理解正在发生的事情变得更加困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've heard you mention that you've observed that every company that runs on Kubernetes ends up building some version of an internal pass that all kind of look roughly the same.
zh: 我听你提到过，你观察到每一家跑在 Kubernetes 上的公司最终都会构建某种版本的内部 pass，而且这些 pass 看起来都大致相同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it that teams end up insisting on building their own thing?
zh: 为什么团队最终都坚持要构建自己的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of reminds me a little bit of in the early days of Auth.
zh: 这让我有点想起 Auth 早期的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every engineer wrote Auth eight different times across every company.
zh: 每家公司里每个工程师都把 Auth 写了八遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And eventually services came out that take that thing off of people's plate.
zh: 最终出现了把这些事情从人们手上接过去的服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: But why is it that we're still in this place where people are writing these internal passes?
zh: 但为什么我们还处于人们仍在编写这些内部 pass 的境地？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a little bit of, well, this is how we used to do it, so why change?
zh: 我认为有一点是，「嗯，我们以前就是这么做的，为什么要改？」

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's also a generational thing.
zh: 还有一代人的因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people learned to build cloud infrastructure using the tools that AWS gave them.
zh: 很多人是使用 AWS 给他们的工具学会构建云基础设施的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Kubernetes was sort of this state that we ended up in.
zh: 然后 Kubernetes 某种程度上是我们最终陷入的这样一种状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you just sort of assume that that is how you always do it or that that's how you will always do it.
zh: 你就某种程度地默认，那就是你一直以来的做法，或者那就是你将来永远的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I also now see from Render's perspective, we actually see teams moving from large Kubernetes clusters to Render because they get all the functionality that they're looking for without having to deal with the complexity of Kubernetes.
zh: 但我现在也从 Render 的角度看到，我们实际上看到团队从大型 Kubernetes 集群迁移到 Render，因为他们得到了他们想要的所有功能，而不必应对 Kubernetes 的复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And interestingly, that's happening more and more now.
zh: 有趣的是，这种情况现在越来越多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Partly because, and I'm sorry to bring up AI again, but so many more people are building so many more applications with AI that this whole notion of statically managing your cluster using a DevOps team is breaking down.
zh: 部分原因是——很抱歉我又要提到 AI——有这么多更多的人在用 AI 构建更多的应用程序，以至于用 DevOps 团队静态管理你的集群这整个理念正在崩塌。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's breaking down very quickly because the DevOps teams are stretched thin beyond capacity everywhere, and they're just trying to keep up with the core application, but then everyone else is like, well, I have this other application I want to stand up.
zh: 它正在非常快地崩塌，因为 DevOps 团队在各处都被拉扯得超出了负荷，他们只是在努力跟上核心应用程序，但其他所有人都在说：「嗯，我有另外一个应用程序想要搭建起来。」

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, good luck because you can only do so much with a small DevOps team or even a large DevOps team.
zh: 那祝你好运，因为一个小 DevOps 团队甚至一个大 DevOps 团队能做的也就这么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think that if you look at sort of the traditional software development lifecycle of discovery, design, implementation, testing, productionization, that kind of thing running in a loop, if historically the coding part, the implementation piece was like kind of slow and hard, the other things around it could kind of be relatively slow because it was not as slow as the thing in the middle, which was actually writing the code.
zh: 我是说，我认为如果你看一下传统的软件开发生命周期——探索、设计、实现、测试、生产化之类的在一个循环中运转——如果从历史上看，编码的部分、实现的环节相对缓慢而艰难，那么围绕它的其他环节可以相对慢一些，因为它没有中间那个环节——也就是真正编写代码——那么慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now we've compressed that time.
zh: 但现在我们把这个时间压缩了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if people generating, instead of having two apps, they're generating, you know, two apps a week.
zh: 所以如果人们在生成,不是拥有两个应用,而是一周生成两个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can slow down the company suddenly becomes the DevOps team and how do you actually run the platform?
zh: 慢下来怎么行,公司突然变成了 DevOps 团队,你到底要怎么运营这个平台?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and that's exactly what we're seeing and it's why Render has grown more in the last two years than in the previous six.
zh: 是的,这正是我们看到的情况,也是 Render 在过去两年里的增长超过之前六年的原因。

zh: 是的，确实有大批人涌入，他们不算 iCoder 的消费者。

speaker: Unknown
en: The people who are technical and who can kind of understand pseudocode, which means they can kind of understand what's happening with Claude.
zh: 这些人有技术背景，能够大致理解伪代码，这意味着他们能够大致理解 Claude 在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then we're also seeing people using Claude and Codex to teach themselves coding because it's now become a lot easier.
zh: 但我们也看到有人在用 Claude 和 Codex 自学编程，因为现在学编程变得容易多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just ask Claude, hey, you did this, explain this to me.
zh: 你可以直接问 Claude,嘿，你做了这个，给我解释一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think Codex also has, or maybe Claude too, they have like a learning mode in them, where instead of just coding it, it will actually teach you along the way.
zh: 而且我认为 Codex 也有，或者可能 Claude 也有，它们内置了某种学习模式，它不只是直接写代码，而是会在过程中真正教会你。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in many ways, I think the definition of a software developer is expanding.
zh: 所以在很多方面，我认为软件开发者的定义正在扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not talking about people who just...
zh: 我说的不是那些只是……

speaker: Unknown
en: want to buy code on places like Lovable or Base44.
zh: 想在 Lovable 或 Base44 这类地方买代码的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm talking about people who want to build apps for their business or internal apps for their business use case or even external apps like product managers are the perfect example where they're technical, they've had maybe a computer science degree, but they haven't been coding professionally.
zh: 我说的是那些想为自己的业务构建应用、为业务使用场景构建内部应用、甚至构建外部应用的人，产品经理就是最好的例子：他们有技术底子，可能读过计算机科学学位，但没有以写代码为职业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, now they can and they are and they're building applications that would be impossible for them to build earlier.
zh: 而现在他们可以了，他们也确实在做，而且在构建一些以前对他们来说不可能构建的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the whole industry and the nature and the number of applications is expanding really, really rapidly.
zh: 所以整个行业以及应用的本质和数量都在非常、非常快速地扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think Render's actually kind of fortunate because we're in the right place at the right time to take advantage of this wave of people who just want an easy place and a fast way to deploy these applications and bring them to the people who want to use them because none of these people are actually going to
zh: 而我认为 Render 其实算是幸运的，因为我们恰好在正确的时间处在正确的位置，能够借助这一波人的浪潮——他们只想要一个简单的地方和一条快速的途径来部署这些应用，并把它们交付给想用的人，因为这些人都不会真的去……

speaker: Unknown
en: to use AWS to deploy their applications.
zh: 用 AWS 来部署他们的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not what they're looking for.
zh: 那不是他们要找的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So many new developers are really being trained on a new kind of cloud as opposed to AWS back in the day.
zh: 所以很多新开发者实际上是在一种新的云上被训练出来的，而不是像当年的 AWS。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think that's exactly right.
zh: 是的，我觉得说得完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, even within an organization I work for, well, one, I'm generating more code than I have in a very long time.
zh: 你知道，即使在我工作的组织内部，第一，我正在生成比很长一段时间以来多得多的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think that's across the board with all the PMs that I work with.
zh: 而且我认为这在我合作的所有 PM 当中是普遍现象。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also I think that we're kind of creating a world where a lot of software is like ephemeral because it's easy to spin up stuff.
zh: 但另外我也认为，我们正在创造一个很多软件像是一次性 ephemeral 一样的世界，因为把东西搭起来太容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I created like a dashboard the other day to measure engagement with a particular product.
zh: 比如我前几天就创建了一个仪表盘，用来衡量某个产品的用户参与度。

speaker: Unknown
en: That I could have had someone within the company build in Tableau or something like that at some point, but I can just spin that up easily using something like Claude Code, run it on render and have that thing ready to go.
zh: 那个东西本来可以让公司里某个人用 Tableau 或类似工具在某时候做出来，但我可以用 Claude Code 这样的东西轻松把它搭起来，跑在 Render 上，然后就立即可用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for two days, and then when I'm done with it, I can throw it away.
zh: 用个两天，等我用完了，我就可以把它扔掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not like the same heavy investment that I spent time on.
zh: 而且这并不像我曾经投入大量时间的那种重度投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's interesting, we're seeing that what you just said about ephemeral applications, we're seeing that people are creating a lot of apps that live for shorter durations.
zh: 有意思的是，我们正看到你刚才说的关于短暂应用的现象，我们看到人们在创建很多生命周期更短的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Render's obviously great for that because you only pay for when the application is live, you don't have to worry about...
zh: Render 显然很适合这一点，因为你只需为应用在线的时间付费，你不用操心……

speaker: Unknown
en: All this other infrastructure just sitting around waiting for you to deploy another app on it.
zh: 所有那些闲置着、等你部署另一个应用的基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then a lot of people are also able to create long running applications that are helping their businesses.
zh: 但同时也有很多人能够创建长期运行的应用来支撑他们的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's really great, really exciting, motivating to be at the center of all of it.
zh: 能处在这一切的中心，真的很棒、很令人兴奋、很受激励。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, again, thank you so much for being here.
zh: 好的，再次非常感谢你能来。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was fantastic.
zh: 这期太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for having me.
zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was a great conversation.
zh: 这是一次很棒的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, cheers.
zh: 好，再见。
